title: Asking for a Drink
label: ch:ar-asking-for-a-drink
canDo: I can name tea, milk, sugar and coffee in Arabic and ask for any of them politely, and I can tell at sight whether an Arabic noun is feminine.

payoff.summary: Say the chapter's drinks and name which of them Arabic built and which it borrowed — ḥalīb from ḥalaba, 'he milked', against shāy and sukkar, which arrived with no root at all — then read the ة off qahwa as a gender marker, place it beside maktaba and as-salāma, and order each drink with min faḍlik, answering ʿafwan.
